newsitem.title: UK: LME copper finishes with foothold above $2,400.
newsitem.headline: LME copper finishes with foothold above $2,400.

text.p: LME copper charged higher on Monday, fuelled by widespread buying and a tight market, but other markets failed to follow in its wake.
Three months copper peaked at $2,415 per tonne in the afternoon, ending the afternoon kerb at $2,409, a gain of $19.
"Everything's looking very positive," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The premium of cash over three months metal ended slightly wider at $62/$66, compared to $55/$60 on Friday evening.
Bits of tightness were appearing in the market and borrowing of the cash/June spread was seen in the morning, traders said.
In the morning, trade profit-taking turned back an initial move above $2,400, but after it was absorbed, widespread buying took prices to fresh highs.
Many in the market were emboldened after funds showed confidence by borrowing to roll over large positions last week, Adams said.
The 1,750-tonne fall in LME stocks, the first in about a week, lent support, while the weaker dollar sparked interest in non-dollar markets.
The next big upside target is $2,440.
Aluminium also made some upside progress, skating to a high of $1,679, but forward selling pushed it back to $1,670 by the close, a $8 gain.
Once prices close above the March 24 high of $1,672, there will not be much in the way of regaining the $1,707 recent peak, Adams said.
"We will see continued producer forward selling into the strength, but the fundamentals are looking quite good," he said.
LME stocks on Monday scored another in a relentless series of falls, this time eroding by 2,600 tonnes.
The other metals were left behind and strayed little from recent ranges.
Nickel climbed to $7,900 resistance before turning back and settling at $7,835 for a $5 gain.
Trade selling and profit taking has been seen in the market, capping gains, but funds still have more buying to do, analysts said.
Lead saw a late bit of strength, ending at its high of $630, a gain of $8.
Prices have edged back above the 10-day moving average but are still well under last week's highs.
After modest consumer buying dries up, prices may be on-line to test the recent low of $615 hit on April 29, analysts said.
Below $615, support was seen at $604 and $597.
Zinc took a rest after sharp gains last week, finishing the day $3 firmer at $1,335.
The market, approaching overbought levels, probably needs to regroup before attacking higher levels again, analysts said.
Tin remained fenced in a narrow trading range, ending barely changed at $5,870, down $10.
Near-term support was pegged at the 100-day moving average at $5,867, with $5,800/20 the next floor.
Alloy ended stronger at $1,520/30, sharply up from $1,500/07.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
